{"fetched_at":"2026-06-12","jd_text":"Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
Location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic’s products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities
- Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
- Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic’s GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
- Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
- Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
- Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
- Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic’s products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have
- 7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
- 3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
- Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
- Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
- Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
- Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
- A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have
- 5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
- Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience.
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience.
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position.
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, Anthropic expects all staff to be in one of its offices at least 25% of the time. Some roles may require more time in office.
Visa sponsorship: Anthropic says it sponsors visas but cannot successfully sponsor every role and candidate.

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships function (GTM context) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic is moving beyond model access into repeatable enterprise adoption. Its public deployment guidance treats implementation as a lifecycle: technical setup, launch and change management, enablement, then scaled adoption.

The operating tension is not simply technical credibility with partners. It is making Claude deployment repeatable across cloud, technology, and services ecosystems while preserving Anthropic’s emphasis on reliable, steerable, and
responsible use.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation and frontier-AI company with a hybrid product, platform, and enterprise-adoption archetype. Its core commercial surfaces span Claude, enterprise offerings, and a platform for building applications
and agents with Claude models.

Its differentiation is closely tied to the company’s stated focus on reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI. That makes deployment quality, customer trust, and implementation discipline part of the commercial product—not merely post-sale
services.

The dominant motion is platform-led but increasingly ecosystem-amplified: Anthropic supplies the models and managed platform; partners help translate them into industry workflows, deployments, and customer outcomes.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic must convert frontier-model demand into durable, production-grade adoption across both direct product use and enterprise implementation. The company’s enterprise materials explicitly frame adoption as organizational change, not a
one-time technical rollout.

This creates a scaling pressure: product teams need consistent deployment feedback, while commercial teams need reusable architectures and partner-led delivery patterns. The decision-rights challenge is balancing central product and safety
standards with field-level flexibility for varied customer environments.

As a public benefit corporation, Anthropic has an additional structural incentive to align growth with its beneficial-AI mission. In enterprise settings, that raises the bar for how use cases, controls, and implementation practices are
represented externally.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Daniela Amodei is a cofounder and president. Their company has been built around the proposition that advanced AI should be reliable, interpretable, and steerable.

Relevant stakeholders are likely to include:
- Partnerships and commercial leadership, which need scalable routes to customer adoption through external ecosystems.
- Product and engineering teams, which need deployment feedback that distinguishes one-off integration requests from repeatable platform needs.
- Enterprise administrators and customer technology leaders, who own identity, access, rollout, governance, training, and adoption inside client organizations.
- Cloud, services, and technology partners, which need clear technical positioning and a viable implementation role around Claude.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic’s platform positions Claude as infrastructure for applications and agents, including managed agent infrastructure. This shifts architecture conversations from isolated prompts toward application design, orchestration, evaluation,
operational controls, and lifecycle management.

Claude Enterprise deployment guidance identifies four practical adoption phases: technical setup, change management and launch, enablement and training, and scaling adoption. That is a strong signal that architecture must be paired with
organizational rollout design.

Claude Code seats appear in Anthropic’s enterprise administration materials, indicating that enterprise adoption can span both business-user workflows and software-development workflows. Partner architectures must therefore account for
different user populations, controls, and value narratives.

The company’s safety-oriented identity means technical recommendations should be credible in both capability and governance terms. The strongest ecosystem patterns will be those that make safe, well-managed adoption easier to reproduce.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly presents a partner network spanning cloud, technology, and services partners. This is not a peripheral referral model: these partner types collectively shape model access, solution design, customer implementation, and
scaled adoption.

Accenture publicly describes its relationship with Anthropic around enterprise AI deployment, productivity, new-product creation, and the combination of Claude with Accenture’s industry and technology expertise. That illustrates the
intended division of labor: Anthropic supplies the AI platform; services partners contextualize and deliver business transformation.

The partner motion requires more than alliance coverage. It depends on:
- Co-selling technical credibility with customers who expect both model expertise and implementation accountability.
- Joint solution patterns that can be reused by industries, practices, and regional delivery teams.
- Enablement that gives partner practitioners a disciplined path from experimentation to deployed customer outcomes.
- A product-feedback loop that carries partner deployment evidence back into platform, tooling, and adoption priorities.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s current public materials show a maturing enterprise operating model: a dedicated partner network, formal enterprise deployment guidance, and a platform positioned for agent and application development.

That combination increases urgency to standardize how external implementers represent Claude in the market. As customers move from experimentation to organizational rollout, inconsistency in partner architectures, enablement, or governance
can become a growth constraint.

Competitive pressure is also architectural rather than purely model-centric. Cloud providers, systems integrators, and technology platforms are all seeking a meaningful role in enterprise AI delivery. Anthropic needs partners to extend
reach without diluting its technical and safety standards.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise AI adoption as a managed operating change, not a standalone model deployment.
- Reusable reference architectures that reduce variance across partner-led implementations.
- Cloud, services, and technology ecosystem fluency across co-sell and delivery motions.
- Technical executive communication that connects platform capabilities to business outcomes.
- Partner enablement systems, practitioner education, and field-ready solution assets.
- Product-feedback mechanisms grounded in real deployment patterns and recurring objections.
- Governance-aware AI architecture, including rollout controls and responsible-use considerations.
- Building technical teams that can operate across commercial urgency and product rigor.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s partner network spans cloud, technology, and services firms, making repeatable technical enablement a strategic scaling issue.
- The enterprise deployment lifecycle signals a focus on adoption after initial access, especially change management, training, and scale.
- Claude’s application and managed-agent platform creates a need for partner architectures beyond basic API integration.
- Accenture’s public positioning points to a delivery model where Anthropic’s platform is paired with partner industry and implementation capability.
- Anthropic’s reliability and steerability focus makes safe deployment practices part of the customer and partner value proposition.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims must come from the governed resume and proof graph.
